data.title: PAT BUNKER STRUCTURAL LOAD 🧱
data.statement:
PAT maps an underground bunker. Each room sits on a level: the surface is level 0, every step deeper (inside parentheses) is <<-1, -2, …>>

Each room has a base load [[b]] and a depth [[d]], where depth is the absolute value of level. The deeper a room, the more weight bears on it — its load doubles for every level down. The load contributed by the room is calculated as:

[[b]] × {{2}}^[[d]]

Room base loads:
{{generator}}={{1}} · {{storage}}={{2}} · {{farm}}={{3}} · {{residence}}={{4}} · {{cameras}}={{5}} · {{security}}={{6}}

Output the <<total load>> of the bunker.

lastVersion.statementHTML:
Goal

PAT maps an underground bunker. Each room sits on a level: the surface is level 0, every step deeper (inside parentheses) is -1, -2, …

Each room has a base load b and a depth d, where depth is the absolute value of level. The deeper a room, the more weight bears on it — its load doubles for every level down. The load contributed by the room is calculated as:

b × 2^d

Room base loads:
generator=1 · storage=2 · farm=3 · residence=4 · cameras=5 · security=6

Output the total load of the bunker.
Input
Line 1: A string S of space-separated room names, ( to go one level deeper, and ) to come back up.
Output
Line 1: An integer, the total structural load of the bunker.
Constraints
1 ≤ length of S ≤ 99
S contains only the room names listed above and the tokens ( and ). The parentheses in S are always balanced and never appear at the beginning of S.
Example
Input
generator storage
Output
3
